workload.fixture: deterministic (PCG-style multiplier stream per layer digest); identical across phases

matched_baselines.description: Same fixture, same budget, same storm, two policies: A = unpinned LRU (no tenant pinning, everyone evicts everyone), B = tenant-0 adapters pinned via pin_adapter().

phase_a_unpinned_lru.note: shared-budget LRU without tenant pinning: the standing storm thrashes every tenant; a page brought in for lookup i is gone before lookup i+1

phase_b_tenant0_pinned.note: pinning one tenant's hot adapters makes its pages immortal under the storm; other tenants keep thrashing on the residual budget

matched_baselines.claim: tenant pinning converts the pinned tenant from 0.0% to 96.9% hit ratio under a standing eviction storm, at zero additional device budget (pages were already resident between lookups; pinning removes their LRU eviction candidacy)

policy_cost.note: fabric-level registry policy cost only: hashing, stats deltas, lease state transitions. No device I/O is simulated; the device-side cost belongs to the engine.

hypotheses.text: unpinned LRU under a standing multi-tenant storm saturates at ~0% hit ratio
hypotheses.expected_failure_mode: if LRU recency (not budget pressure) dominates, hit ratio stays materially positive

hypotheses.text: tenant pinning lifts the pinned tenant to near-100% hit ratio at unchanged budget
hypotheses.expected_failure_mode: if pinning starves its own admissions (pin-all-pages pathology), ratio drops or budget overflows
hypotheses.observed: confirmed: 248/256 = 96.9%; residual misses are the first-pass admissions per storm round

hypotheses.text: policy-layer cost stays sub-microsecond per lookup
hypotheses.expected_failure_mode: salted key computation or stats bookkeeping dominating would push this to µs+

hypotheses.text: salt isolation: a foreign salt cannot resolve a registered adapter
hypotheses.observed: confirmed: UnknownAdapter error asserted in the bench

out_of_scope: runtime hot-swap of adapter weights into the attention path
device memory management and device-side I/O (this is a policy layer, not the engine)
multi-GPU placement and NUMA-aware page ownership
pin budget negotiation between tenants (a single demo tenant is pinned; a quota arbiter is future work)
replication: git checkout the PR head; cargo run --release -p hanzo-kv-fabric --example lora_paging_bench
